## What

To gate a dev-only UI surface so it ships in the desktop **dev** shell but is
**absent from the production build**, gate on
`import.meta.env.MODE !== 'production'` — **not** `import.meta.env.DEV`.

```tsx
// ✅ shows in the desktop dev shell, tree-shaken out of production
const DevAdminRail =
  import.meta.env.MODE !== 'production'
    ? lazy(() => import('../components/dev-admin-rail/DevAdminRail'))
    : null;

// ❌ NEVER appears in the desktop — DEV is false in a `vite build`
const DevAdminRail = import.meta.env.DEV ? lazy(...) : null;
```

## Why (the trap)

Vite ties `import.meta.env.DEV` / `.PROD` to the **command** (`vite` serve vs
`vite build`), while `.MODE` follows `--mode`. The desktop's three run modes
(see [Dev modes](/internal/docs/desktop/dev-modes)) are:

| Run mode | command | `MODE` | `DEV` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bin/desktop-dev` (HMR) | `vite` (serve) | `development` | `true` |
| `bin/desktop-dev-nohmr` (rebuild-watch) | `vite build --watch --mode development` | `development` | **`false`** |
| shipped (`tauri build`) | `vite build` | `production` | `false` |

`bin/desktop-dev-nohmr` is the **default** `npm run dev` for the desktop, and it
is a `vite build` — so `import.meta.env.DEV` is `false` there. A `DEV`-gated
surface compiles away and **never appears in the desktop you're testing in**,
even though you're "in dev". `MODE` is the only flag that is `development` in
**both** dev shells and `production` only in the shipped build.

(Empirically confirmed on this repo's rolldown-vite: a `DEV`-gated rail was absent
from both a `--mode development` build and a production build; the `MODE`-gated
rail was present in the dev build and absent in the prod build.)

## How to verify the gate (build-grep)

`MODE` is a static string Vite replaces at build time, so a `MODE`-gated lazy
chunk is dead code in prod — Rollup drops it. Prove both directions by building
to throwaway dirs and grepping for a marker unique to your surface:

```bash
cd apps/operator-vite
npx vite build                          --outDir /tmp/p --emptyOutDir   # production
npx vite build --mode development       --outDir /tmp/d --emptyOutDir   # dev
grep -rho "<your-unique-class-or-string>" /tmp/p/   # → 0 (absent in prod)
grep -rho "<your-unique-class-or-string>" /tmp/d/   # → >0 (present in dev)
```

Run the two builds **sequentially** to separate `--outDir`s — concurrent
`vite build`s share the vite cache dir and cross-contaminate each other's output.

## Two more gotchas this surfaced

- **CSS imported by a dead lazy module still leaks.** Vite eagerly collects a
  `import './x.css'` into the output stylesheet even when the importing module is
  a tree-shaken dynamic chunk — the JS goes, the class names stay. Carry dev-only
  CSS as a JS string injected via `<style>{CSS}</style>` (a JS import tree-shakes
  with the dead module) instead of a `.css` import. (FeaturesAdmin's inline
  `<style>` pattern, for the same reason.)
- **Pick a unique class prefix.** `pc-dev-*` is already heavily used by the
  `/dev` page (`pc-dev-rail-*`, `pc-dev-panel`, `pc-dev-row`, `pc-dev-kv`).
  Reusing it bleeds CSS onto that page. The dev admin rail uses `pcdar*`.

## Where this came from

The dev admin rail (`apps/operator-vite/src/components/dev-admin-rail/`, plan
`dev-admin-sidebar-2026-06-05`). Its plan named `import.meta.env.DEV`; that would
have made the rail invisible in the very desktop it's meant for. The mount in
`apps/operator-vite/src/routes/__root.tsx` carries the corrected gate + rationale.
